6ae03b292672:
🌼 A new icon of Saint Charalambos.

🌿 Saint Charalambos the Hieromartyr, protector of the poor and the sick and deliverer from plague, a saint to whom the Romanian peasant (especially in 18th–19th century Transylvania) once prayed for protection from plague, cholera, typhoid fever and the other epidemics that used to ravage people. The same Romanian peasant “painted” Saint Charalambos in countless icons on glass. One of them is the model for the icon I am showing you today (workshop in Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century)

🎨 About the icon: the icon shows Saint Charalambos binding the plague, and so saving the city. Charalambos is shown in the usual way (standing, dressed in robe, mantle and omophorion, with the holy book and halo, giving a blessing), trampling the plague, which is bound by a chain fastened to his belt. The plague, carrying a scythe, has the face of a horned man. On either side of the saint, in the background, the image is enriched by a cityscape with palaces and fortified walls. The ground is rendered by bands of colour bearing hatching, crosses and flowers. From high in the sky the scene is watched over by Jesus, who blesses him, and by an angel holding out a wreath of flowers to him. They are seated on clouds. On the light-blue background are large unoutlined flowers and black stars (source of the description: the National Museum of Art of Romania)

4b97da5d03b8:
Saint Martin of Tours ~ Icon painted on glass

Saint Martin is celebrated on 11 November, and also on 4 July (the date he was raised to bishop, in 371).

Doxologia.ro:
“ Saint Martin is one of the most popular saints in the Catholic Church, and he is also venerated as a saint in the Orthodox Church. He was born around the year 316 in Savaria (today Szombathely, in Hungary), the son of a pagan Roman tribune, but he received a Christian education in Pavia (his father's home town), becoming a catechumen at the age of ten. Obeying his father, he had to enlist in the Roman imperial army, serving in the bodyguard of Emperor Constantius II.
Posted to the cavalry legions at Amiens (in Gaul), he once met a nearly naked beggar at the city gate. Moved with pity, he cut his cloak in two with his sword and gave half of it to the man in need. The following night he dreamt of the Lord Christ, who revealed to him that He Himself had been present in the form of the poor man.”

The icon we are showing you today was inspired by the scene described above.

The icon is not available; it was ordered as a gift.

 “Saint Martin was born around the year 316 in Savaria (in the province of Pannonia, today Szombathely in Hungary), the son of a pagan Roman tribune, but he received a Christian education in Pavia (his father's home town), becoming a catechumen at the age of ten. Obeying his father, he had to enlist in the Roman imperial army, serving in the bodyguard of Emperor Constantius II. Posted to the cavalry legions at Amiens (in Gaul), he once met a nearly naked beggar at the city gate. Moved with pity, he cut his cloak (called “cappa” in Latin) in two with his sword and gave half of it to the man in need. The following night he dreamt of the Lord Christ, who revealed to him that He Himself had been present in the form of the poor man.” (source of the description: doxologia.ro)

7b7da5e5c52f:
2 July: the veneration of the icon of the Mother of God “the Nursing Mother” (Galaktotrophousa, the Nourisher of Life)

“The Mother of God is the true Mother of Life, our guiding mother and intercessor. She who nourishes all of us who ask for her help in need. Unconditionally, at any moment and at any hour of the day or night!” (Justinian of Maramureș and Sătmar)

Over time, this icon has been made on wood or on glass, in various versions. One of the oldest such depictions of the Mother of God is on the Holy Mountain of Athos (Hilandar Monastery); other depictions of this theme can be admired in manuscripts and, of course, many delightful depictions are found in the icons on glass of the Transylvanian icon painters, one of them (workshop in Șcheii Brașovului, second half of the 19th century) being the model after which we made this icon in our workshop.

The icon is not available. If you would like a similar icon, contact me.
0f9031fde40d:
29 June: «The Holy Apostles Peter and Paul»

 In Orthodox iconography (and so also in the icon painted on glass in our workshop, which we are showing you today) the two apostles are painted together: Peter holding a bunch of keys and Paul a sword. What is the meaning of these two elements, what do these objects signify?

Fr. Constantin Sturzu explains: «The keys that Saint Peter holds are “the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven”; they unlock the gates of Paradise, but only through the sacrament of repentance, or confession.
The sword means the diligent preaching of the word of God; so if we receive the word of God, even if it stings at first like a cut from a sword, it then opens the gates of eternity to us, just as a key opens the door of a house.»

Happy name day to all who celebrate!
49604ebe267a:
24 June 2023: «The Holy Trinity»

• “The Holy Trinity is the supreme mystery of existence, which explains everything, and without which nothing can be explained.” (Father Dumitru Stăniloae)

• On the Monday after Pentecost Sunday (which is dedicated to glorifying the Holy Trinity), we are showing you a few icons painted on glass in our workshop – after different models – whose common theme is «The Holy Trinity and the Coronation of the Mother of God».

• The scene shows the Holy Trinity (the spiritual unity of the three divine persons): Jesus Christ carrying the Cross of the crucifixion, God the Father with the orb and sceptre (the insignia of the Almighty), and the Holy Spirit (as a white dove framed by the sun) sending down His blessing. The first two hold a crown above the head of the Virgin Mary (kneeling, with her hands crossed on her chest). The figures are ”held up” by clouds.

• These icons were made to order, so they are not available. If you would like an icon on this theme, contact me to settle the details.

4130c85923db:
The Holy Archangels Michael and Gabriel – icon on glass

• Michael, whose name means “the power of God”, is the commander of the heavenly hosts and the first of the choir of the Holy Archangels.
• Gabriel, whose name means “man of God”, is the archangel of good tidings; his mission is to announce to people the great mysteries of God.
• Both are leaders of the choirs of angels and guides of souls towards Paradise.

• With great joy I worked on a new icon of the two Holy Archangels; this time it was wanted for a little home in Tulcea, where another icon painted in our workshop, the Table of Paradise, was waiting for it.
